# Another Agent Skills

> An open-source framework of 58 composable skills and mechanical enforcement that turns AI coding agents into disciplined senior engineers. Most skill libraries sell capability; this one sells discipline you can verify.

Key facts (citable):

- License: MIT. No subscriptions, no paid tiers, no lock-in.
- Skills: 58, mapped to a six-phase lifecycle (Define, Plan, Build, Verify, Review, Ship), with 153 guides and an eval for each.
- Skills reference: every skill's what, activation trigger, use and non-use, grouped by category, in EN and ES.
- Enforcement is three layers: L1 local git hooks (fast, advisory feedback), L2 a required remote `gates` status check the committer cannot skip, L3 CODEOWNERS review of sensitive paths. L2 and L3 require GitHub.
- The core rule: a code change with no matching test is blocked, locally and remotely.
- The agent never runs `git commit` or `git push`; the human does.
- Harness: six layers around the model: instructions, tools, sandboxes, orchestration, guardrails, observability.
- Agents: 15 detected, including OpenCode, Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Aider, Kiro, Zed. Any agent that reads AGENTS.md is supported.
- Stacks: Node, Rust, Python, Go, Ruby, Dart, or any stack. `init-agents` writes STACK_CONFIG.md.
- Install channels: `git clone` + `install.sh` (live), pinned `curl` bootstrap from the latest release (live), npm (live).
- Works offline after install; no external runtime dependencies; no trackers.
- Tutorials: five bilingual walkthroughs (first gated commit, wire remote enforcement, start without git, migrate a legacy project, move to another machine).
- Git flows: no git (convention only), local git (L1), git + GitHub (L1/L2/L3), git later (re-run `init-agents` after `git init` and after adding the remote).
